Critics, including the Lausanne statement, say it treats faith as a technique for manipulating God, turns the tithe into an investment, implies that the poor and the sick lack faith, and often enriches the preacher as well.

At its strongest, it points out that Jesus and His disciples had empty hands and that Jesus told the rich man to sell everything. The monastic traditions bear real witness to the beauty of this path. Critics say it is a calling for some, and that making it the universal standard looks down on all that God created and overlooks the real suffering of the poor.

God is the owner and people are stewards. The wealthy need not be ashamed and must not be proud; those without money are not second-class. The main challenge: this view can easily turn into pretty words that change nothing.

blocks.h: Most of the income studies above come from the United States and measure moods and evaluations on questionnaires. “Happiness” is also not the same as the Bible’s joy or peace, and these tools cannot measure a person’s relationship with God. To use them either to endorse or to demolish faith goes beyond what the data can say.
Let’s look at each claim separately and mark how certain it is.
Kahneman and Deaton analyzed more than 450,000 US survey responses and reported that life evaluation rises with income, while mood levels off at about US$75,000.

A later adversarial-collaboration reanalysis found that the leveling off occurs mainly among the least happy people, and that for most people happiness keeps rising with the logarithm of income. The research draws mainly on American respondents.

Swedish lottery big-prize winners still reported higher overall life satisfaction more than ten years later, but the effects on happiness and mental health were much smaller. Financial satisfaction may be the main mediator.
Materialistic values are associated with lower subjective well-being; spending on others is associated with well-being. Correlation alone cannot settle the direction of cause.

People have a longing that money and achievement cannot fill, which fits the observations of Ecclesiastes. This longing does not by itself prove God; it only makes Jesus’ words worth listening to seriously.

The Lausanne statement represents the position of many evangelicals: material things are good gifts from God, but wealth is not necessarily a sign of blessing, and poverty, illness and early death are not necessarily a curse or a sign of weak faith.
Where was the man a fool?

Jesus told of a rich man. He did not steal and he did not rob; his harvest simply grew out of his own fields. Today he would be a successful person who makes good plans. His problem hides in his talking to himself. In the few short sentences of the Chinese Union Version, the word “I” appears five times, and God and other people not once.

“But God said to him, ‘You foolish one, tonight your soul is required of you. The things which you have prepared—whose will they be?’So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.”

Paul’s words are also often misquoted. What he speaks of is the love of money; money itself is not sin. He also says that God “richly provides us with everything to enjoy.” God’s goodness is real, and even abundance is His gift. God’s righteousness is real too, so wealth gained by oppression may never be called a blessing.
Charge those who are rich in this present age that they not be arrogant, nor have their hope set on the uncertainty of riches, but on the living God, who richly provides us with everything to enjoy;

The gospel turns all this completely over. The world sets your price by how much you earn and how much you sell. The price God paid for you was His Son. Your worth was already set on the cross, and no report card can change it.

knowing that you were redeemed, not with corruptible things like silver or gold, from the useless way of life handed down from your fathers, but with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish or spot, the blood of Christ,
For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that you through his poverty might become rich.

Open last month’s bills or your calendar. Circle the one entry that makes your heart feel most settled, then circle the one that makes you most anxious. Look at them quietly for a minute and ask: which of these are my “barns”?
Reflect: if today no one knew my savings, my job title or my children’s grades, who would I be? How much peace would I have left?

Pray: Heavenly Father, You richly provide us with everything to enjoy, and I thank You for all You have given me. Forgive me for staking my worth on numbers and titles, and for using achievement to settle my account with my parents and with myself. Lord Jesus, You became poor for me. Be my true wealth, so that my hands can grasp and also let go. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Let Jesus reign: money is a good servant and does not belong on the throne. Before every big decision, ask the Lord first, and then check the account.
Shift your perspective: move from the human, temporary measuring stick to God’s eternal one. Today’s job title will retire, but the kindness shown to a person today will not be wasted.
People matter more than tasks: no performance is worth trading away your family and your health. Relationships matter more than things.

blocks.h: This week: find a person or a need and quietly give an amount of money or time that you can slightly feel. Do it anonymously and do not post about it. Then write down what came up in your heart as you let go.
Pass it on: if you could not mention your income, your job title or your children’s grades, how would you introduce yourself?
Quiz

quiz.q: What did the 2023 adversarial collaboration conclude about income and happiness?
o: Money cannot buy happiness at all
Only the least happy group levels off after a certain income, while everyone else’s happiness keeps rising
People earning more than US$75,000 a year become unhappy
quiz.e: The two camps reanalyzed the data together and corrected the earlier claim. This is American data, and it measures mood, not a relationship with God.

quiz.q: What was the key reason Jesus called the rich man a “fool”?
o: He laid up treasure for himself and was not rich toward God
His land was acquired by dubious means
Being rich is itself a sin
quiz.e: Luke 12:21. The parable never mentions stealing or robbing; his problem was a life with nothing left in it but himself.

quiz.q: Which of the following comes closest to the Lausanne statement’s criticism of prosperity theology?
o: Material things have nothing to do with God’s blessing
Christians should give up all their possessions
God’s power cannot be manipulated by technique, and poverty and illness are not necessarily a lack of faith
quiz.e: The statement affirms that material things belong to God’s blessing, but refuses to treat wealth as the necessary sign of being blessed.

units.title: Forgiveness: Letting Others Go, and Letting Yourself Go
units.sub: Forgiving is writing a bad debt off your heart. It does not ask you to move back into the unsafe building.

share.v: And be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.

blocks.h: On October 2, 2006, in an Amish schoolhouse in Pennsylvania, a gunman killed five girls, the youngest only 6 years old, and seriously wounded five others, and then took his own life. Before the world had caught its breath, the Amish had already extended forgiveness to the killer’s widow and family.

Ten years later reporters went back. The grief was still there, and one survivor still sat in a wheelchair and needed long-term care. A father who lost a child said that he had been freed from anger and bitterness, but not freed from the pain. So forgiveness is not an eraser. Then what is it?
Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.”
If you are being hurt right now, please read this part first

Your safety comes before every single sentence in this unit. If someone at home hits you, threatens you or controls you, or if someone is hurting you or your children, forgiveness is not the question you need to answer first. Please find a safe place and professional help first. You do not have to forgive first, and you do not have to check first whether you are “spiritual” enough.

Taiwan: 113 Protection Hotline (24 hours); call 110 if you are in immediate danger. Singapore: National Anti-Violence and Sexual Harassment Helpline 1800-777-0000; call 999 if you are in immediate danger. Malaysia: Talian Kasih 15999 (24 hours). New Zealand: Women’s Refuge 0800 733 843, Are You OK 0800 456 450. Elsewhere, please find a local protection hotline or call the police.

Nearly one in three women worldwide experiences partner violence or sexual violence in her lifetime; the World Health Organization estimated in 2025 that this is about 840 million people. Men and children can be victims too. You are not alone, and it is not your fault.
What forgiveness is not

items: It is not saying “it’s nothing.” You forgive precisely because the thing was wrong. If there were no wrong, there would be nothing to forgive.
It is not reconciliation. Forgiving a person can be done alone; reconciliation takes two people, and the other person must truly change.
It is not restoring trust. Trust is rebuilt slowly through time and facts, and in some situations it should not be rebuilt.
It is not refusing to call the police or to hold anyone accountable. Legal responsibility still stands. Protecting the next person is love too.
It is not forgetting, and there is no deadline. No one can rush you. The deeper the wound, the longer the road may be.

blocks.h: The psychologist Everett Worthington, who has studied forgiveness for decades, says that forgiveness happens inside your own skin, while whether justice is done is another matter. A person can forgive an abuser and at the same time refuse to reconcile with someone who is still dangerous.

In accounting there is a move called “writing off a bad debt.” The money really is owed, and the books record it clearly. I simply stop phoning every day to collect it and stop letting it take over my life. Writing off a bad debt does not mean I will lend him another million. A criminal case can still go forward.

Or think of a building wrecked by an earthquake. You can stop splashing paint at the developer’s door every day, and that is your own business. Whether to move back in is for a structural engineer to say. If the engineer has not signed off, anyone who urges you to move back is harming you. Forgiveness is the first; reconciliation is the second.
What forgiveness is

It is a gradual process: acknowledging the harm, facing the anger, and then handing over the right to collect the debt and to take revenge. Researchers often separate two layers: first a decision not to retaliate, with the change in feelings usually coming much more slowly. Worthington’s five REACH steps are Recall the hurt, Empathize, give forgiveness as an Altruistic gift, Commit, and Hold on. His own mother was killed in a home invasion; the police believed they knew who did it but never secured a prosecution. He says he forgave quickly, but he had been studying forgiveness for years, and no one should use that as a standard for measuring themselves.

A 2014 meta-analysis showed that psychological interventions to promote forgiveness do help. In a 2024 randomized controlled trial of 4,598 people in Hong Kong, Indonesia, Colombia, South Africa and Ukraine, a self-guided workbook lowered feelings of unforgiveness after two weeks, with a much smaller effect on depression and anxiety. The follow-up was only two weeks, the participants were mostly young women, and all the data were self-reported, so the results should not be overstated.
Forgiveness has a shadow side

In 2011 James McNulty followed newlywed couples and found that when one spouse was more inclined to forgive, the partner’s verbal and physical aggression was more likely to continue. Robert Enright, a pioneer of forgiveness research, criticized the study: the questionnaire had only five items, the scenarios were mostly hypothetical, and “forgiveness” was never defined, so these respondents may have been merely tolerating or condoning. The one point both sides agree on: treating forgiveness as condoning lets people keep getting hurt.

Another study interviewed women in domestic violence shelters about how forgiveness related to their intention to return to their partners. So to a person who is being abused, saying “You must forgive him and go back” may send her back into danger. The church must never say this.
The truth cannot be skipped either

South Africa’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission was established under a 1995 law by the Mandela government, with Archbishop Tutu as chair. Those who applied for amnesty had to disclose the facts fully, and the crime had to be linked to a political aim. Of 7,112 applications, 849 were granted and 5,392 were refused. It let victims speak publicly about their experiences for the first time and helped secure a peaceful transition. At the same time, the family of Steve Biko felt that they had been robbed of their right to seek justice, and took the case to the highest court. The controversy has never ended, and it reminds us that reconciliation at the national level cannot be used to make demands on the heart of any single victim.

items.n: Forgiveness is not conditional on the offender’s repentance
items.h: On the cross Jesus asked the Father to forgive the very people who were hurting Him, and Mark 11:25 says to forgive whenever you stand praying. This way the victim does not have to wait for the offender, and the heart can be set free first.

Luke 17:3 says, “If he repents, forgive him.” God’s forgiveness of people also calls for repentance. Those who hold this view say that until the other person repents, we lay down revenge and bitterness and hand the case to God, and the completion of forgiveness and reconciliation wait for the other to turn back.
Neither wants people to take revenge, neither asks the victim to pretend nothing happened, and neither asks for reconciliation to come before safety.

blocks.h: Let’s keep the facts, the research and the beliefs apart.

The shooting at the Amish school in Nickel Mines, Pennsylvania, on October 2, 2006 left five girls dead and five seriously wounded. The Amish community quickly extended forgiveness to the killer’s family, and ten years later was still bearing the pain.
South Africa’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission received about 7,112 amnesty applications and granted 849; the Biko family publicly opposed this and brought a lawsuit.
The World Health Organization estimated in 2025 that about 840 million women, nearly one in three, have experienced partner violence or sexual violence in their lifetime.
Structured forgiveness interventions can reduce feelings of unforgiveness, with a smaller effect on depression and anxiety; long-term effects remain to be studied.
The relationship between a tendency to forgive and a partner’s continued aggression is still disputed: one study found them related, and its measurement has been criticized.
Christians are able to forgive because they have first been forgiven by God, and they trust that the final judgment is in God’s hands. This is a confession of faith that research cannot verify.

The story of Corrie ten Boom is also often told. Her sister died in the Ravensbrück concentration camp. In 1947, after she spoke in Munich, a man who had been a guard at the camp held out his hand and asked for her forgiveness. By her own account her heart was cold, and she could only ask God to help her lift her hand. Only then did she feel warmth flood in. This is her personal testimony; please do not take that warm flood as a standard every person must have.
The man who owed ten thousand talents

When Peter asked how many times to forgive, Jesus told a parable. The Chinese Union Version’s “ten million taels of silver” is, in the original, ten thousand talents, and the “ten taels of silver” is a hundred denarii. By the usual conversion the first is about 600,000 times the second. The point of the parable falls on the man who was released from an astronomical debt: grace can flow through us, or we can block it.

Then his lord called him in and said to him, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt because you begged me. Shouldn’t you also have had mercy on your fellow servant, even as I had mercy on you?’

These words are not meant to hurry the victim. In the same chapter Jesus first teaches “show him his fault,” then taking others along, then telling the church. Sin has to be named. Nor does God tell anyone to stand and take a beating: David dodged Saul’s spear and fled that night, Paul was let down over the city wall in a basket by the disciples, and Jesus passed through the midst of those who wanted to throw Him off a cliff.
Saul sought to pin David to the wall with the spear, but he slipped away out of Saul’s presence; and he stuck the spear into the wall. David fled and escaped that night.

The Bible tells us not to take revenge ourselves, because there is One who will. God’s justice is not absent, and He has also appointed authorities to punish those who do evil. Handing the case to God and handing it to the court do not conflict.
Don’t seek revenge yourselves, beloved, but give place to God’s wrath. For it is written, “Vengeance belongs to me; I will repay, says the Lord.”

The cross is where justice and love meet. Sin was not lightly passed over; Christ bore it Himself. And He did not merely die for the offender; He Himself was the one wronged. So when people covered in scars come before Him, they will not hear “it’s nothing.”
When he was cursed, he didn’t curse back. When he suffered, he didn’t threaten, but committed himself to him who judges righteously.
Letting yourself go too

For some people, the one they cannot forgive is themselves. If you have truly hurt someone, please confess, take responsibility and make amends as best you can, and do not press the other person to forgive you quickly. Then return the authority to condemn to God. People who were wronged often blame themselves too. Those things were not your fault. You do not need to be forgiven; you need to be comforted.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

Take a sheet of paper and write down a name you still cannot let go of, or your own name. You do not have to finish anything today, and you do not have to feel anything right away. Just lay this paper before the Lord for one minute. If the person who comes to mind is dangerous, write “seek safety” beside the name.
Reflect: is my heart still holding court? Which part of this case am I willing to hand to the Lord who judges righteously? And which step is mine to take by going to find someone to help?

Pray: Lord Jesus, You know what wounds I have borne, and You were wounded to the very end. I bring this account to You. I may not be able to let go yet, so please help me. Protect those who are in danger now and give them courage to ask for help. Forgive me also for the ways I have hurt others, so that I no longer act as my own prosecutor. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Jesus is my example: He forgave people, and He also committed Himself to the One who judges righteously. At times He also left a place of danger. To follow Him is to follow all of Him.
Letting God be God: the judge’s seat is God’s. When I lay down the gavel, I carry one less case that sits in court every day in my heart.

Selflessness does not mean being trampled on: selflessness is no longer making yourself the center, and it does not cancel your dignity or your boundaries. Everyone was bought with the precious blood of Christ, and that includes you.

blocks.h: This week: take just one small step. Tell a trustworthy, mature Christian or a counseling professional that there is an account in your heart you cannot let go of. If you are the one who hurt someone, write down the responsibility that is yours, and do not rush to send it to the other person. First think about how to avoid causing further harm.
Pass it on: is there something you badly want to let go of, but you feel that letting go would be saying it doesn’t matter?
Quiz

quiz.q: Which of the following best matches this unit’s account of forgiveness?
o: Once you have forgiven, you should move back in together right away
Forgiveness can be done alone; reconciliation depends on whether the other person truly changes and whether it is safe
Forgiveness means you may not call the police
quiz.e: Forgiveness and reconciliation are two different things, and safety always comes first.

quiz.q: What did David do when Saul threw his spear?
o: Stayed and kept enduring
Took revenge in the same way
Dodged it and fled that night
quiz.e: 1 Samuel 19:10. The Bible does not ask victims to stay in danger to prove their faith.

quiz.q: Which statement about the 2024 five-country REACH randomized controlled trial is correct?
o: The workbook lowered feelings of unforgiveness, but the follow-up was only two weeks and the effect on depression and anxiety was smaller
It proved that forgiveness can cure depression
Its participants were mainly victims of domestic violence
quiz.e: Not overstating is honesty. The participants were a community sample of people who had been hurt by others.

units.title: Love and Family
units.sub: Home can be the warmest place and the most painful place; the Father in heaven understands both.

share.v: We love him, because he first loved us.

blocks.h: In 1938 Harvard University began following 724 people, and has kept at it for more than eighty years. The researchers eventually looked back and asked: which measurement at age fifty best shows who will be healthy and happy at eighty? They had bet on cholesterol and blood pressure. The winner was satisfaction with relationships, especially marriage.
Yet under the same roof there can also lie the deepest wounds of a lifetime. Why does the family have so much power?
God sets the lonely in families. He brings out the prisoners with singing,
One sneer costs more than you think

In 1992 the psychologists John Gottman and Robert Levenson observed couples as they talked through a conflict, then followed up 73 couples four years later. Couples whose relationships stayed stable showed a ratio of positive to negative behavior close to 5 to 1; couples heading toward instability had a ratio of only about 1 to 1.

The Gottman Institute later named the four patterns that hurt a relationship most “the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse”: criticism, contempt, defensiveness and stonewalling. Contempt is the most destructive of them.

A good relationship is like a pot of old braising sauce, whose flavor is built slowly by adding a little each day. A “thank you,” a cup of warm water, a “you’ve worked hard today”: these are all ingredients. Contempt is like a spoonful of dish soap. Once it goes in, no amount of ingredients can cover the taste.
The family we came from: old pipes we cannot see

In 2023 the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention compiled surveys from 2011 to 2020: 63.9% of American adults had at least one adverse experience in childhood (such as abuse, witnessing domestic violence, or parental conflict), and 17.3% had four or more. Such experiences are clearly associated with adult risks such as depression and addiction.

The family we came from is like the plumbing of an old house. Usually you cannot see it, but when the water pressure rises, it leaks. If you pretend nothing is leaking, the ceiling will come down sooner or later. Tearing down the whole house is not the only answer either. Find someone who knows the work, repair it one section at a time, and the house can still be lived in.
If there is violence at home

The World Health Organization’s 2025 estimate: nearly one in three women worldwide, about 840 million, has experienced partner violence or sexual violence in her lifetime. Men and children can be victims too. If this is your situation, it is not your fault, and it is not a cross you are required to carry. Your safety comes first. In Taiwan you can call the 113 Protection Hotline (24 hours, toll-free), and if life is in immediate danger call 110. Elsewhere, please call your local emergency number or domestic violence helpline.
The two faces of filial piety

The Taiwanese scholar Kuang-Hui Yeh and Olwen Bedford proposed the “dual filial piety” model: “reciprocal filial piety,” which grows out of affection, and “authoritarian filial piety,” which grows out of the demands of role and authority. One study found that among Chinese adolescents the former is associated with fewer depressive symptoms and the latter with the opposite. Both are called filial piety, but one comes from love and the other from fear, and they taste very different.

Jesus took filial piety very seriously. He rebuked the religious people who used the label “given to God” to avoid supporting their parents (Mark 7:9-13), and while hanging on the cross He arranged for His disciple to care for His mother (John 19:26-27). He also said that we must not love our parents more than Him (Matthew 10:37). Taken together, filial piety has an order: when God’s place is given to God, parents no longer have to be obeyed as gods, and can instead be truly loved.
How should we read the “submission” passages?

Ephesians 5 is the marriage passage most debated within evangelicalism. The two main readings are both held by brothers and sisters who take the Bible seriously. The passage opens with “mutual submission,” and what it commands husbands is a self-giving love modeled on Christ’s giving of Himself for the church.

items.h: Husband and wife are equally honored before God, with differing roles: the husband takes up the responsibility of leadership with self-giving love, and the wife willingly responds. A representative work is the collection edited by John Piper and Wayne Grudem.

Husband and wife are equally honored and also submit to one another in Christ, with leadership shared according to gifts and circumstances; the household order in the text is the gospel’s transformation of the culture of that day, with the direction being mutual self-giving. Christians for Biblical Equality (CBE) is a representative organization.

blocks.h: We do not rule between them here. Whichever reading is taken, this passage can never become an excuse for violence, control or humiliation.
Research can tell us a great deal, but no single number can pass a verdict on your family.

Long-term follow-up found that satisfaction with relationships in midlife is associated with health and happiness in later life. This is observational research with an American sample, and it cannot be put as relationships “determining” lifespan.

In the 1992 study, stable couples had a positive-to-negative ratio of about 5 to 1. The sample was only 73 American couples, so it should not be treated as a formula for everyone. The popular claim that you can tell who will divorce at a glance is exaggerated, and the Gottman Institute itself clarifies that one can only say a couple’s behavior resembles that of the group in the study who later divorced.

Adverse childhood experiences are quite common among American adults and are associated with many health risks in adulthood. The classic 1998 study included 9,508 respondents, and more than half reported at least one category.
These risks are associations at the group level and cannot predict any one person’s life. Someone who was hurt is not therefore destined to hurt others.

Intimate partner violence is a global public health problem: the WHO estimates that about 316 million women experienced physical or sexual violence from a partner in the past 12 months, about 11% of women aged 15 and over.

The human longing to be loved unconditionally points to a Creator who is Himself love, and the best homes on earth are a reflection of that home. This is an inference of faith; research can neither prove nor disprove it.
For some, the word “Father” hurts to hear

If your father was absent, harsh, or even hurt you, hearing “Heavenly Father” may not feel warm. God does not blame you for that hesitation. The Bible does not ask you to imagine God after the pattern of your earthly father. It lets you see that earthly parents can fail, and that He catches you.
When my father and my mother forsake me, then Yahweh will take me up.
Jesus told of a father. The son had squandered the family property and turned back, and while he was still far away, that father ran to embrace him, before a single word of rebuke had been said.
But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him.
The price of this love is written on the cross. Christ gave Himself so that we who left home would have a road back, and we come back not as hired servants but as children.
For you didn’t receive the spirit of bondage again to fear, but you received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, “Abba! Father!”

To friends who are single, divorced, widowed or without children: in God’s family you are not missing a piece. Jesus Himself never married, and pointing to those who follow Him, He said that whoever does the will of His Father in heaven “is my brother, and sister, and mother” (Matthew 12:50).
Draw a map of your home in your mind. Which room is the warmest? Which door has always been closed? Lay this map honestly before God, without tidying it up first.
Reflect: at home, am I in a hurry to prove I am right, or willing to put myself down first? Which old wound am I carrying that I have not yet let God touch?

Pray: Heavenly Father, thank You for loving me first. You know how much warmth my home holds, and how much pain. Heal the places I cannot put into words. Give me wisdom to tell what to forgive and what to ask help for, and teach me to love those around me with the self-giving love of Christ. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: The order of relationships: God first, then myself, then people, and tasks last. Settle your heart before God first, and when you get home you will not use your family as an outlet for your feelings.

920 starts at home: treat your spouse, parents and children as my 2, lay down the 0 of “I must win,” and let the fruit of the Spirit, such as patience, kindness and gentleness, grow at the dinner table.
People matter more than tasks: the dishes can wait, and the homework questions can wait. Today, first look into the other person’s eyes and ask how they are doing.

blocks.h: This week: every day, say one specific word of thanks to a family member (not “you’re great,” but “thank you for waiting up for me last night”). If home makes you feel afraid, change this week’s action to one thing: tell a trusted person about your situation, or call a professional helping agency.
Pass it on: “If you could say one thing about family to your childhood self, what would you say?”
Quiz

quiz.q: In Gottman and Levenson’s 1992 study, what was the approximate ratio of positive to negative interactions among stable couples?
o: 1 to 1
5 to 1
20 to 1
quiz.e: About 5 to 1. The sample was small, so treat it as a reminder, not a formula.

quiz.q: How did Jesus treat His mother on the cross?
o: He arranged for a disciple to take her home and care for her
He asked her to leave the place of execution
He did not mention her
quiz.e: John 19:26-27: even in His suffering, He cared for His mother.

quiz.q: If violence is happening at home, what does this unit recommend?
o: Keep enduring for the sake of your witness
Pray more and tell no one
Safety first, and seek professional help
quiz.e: First Corinthians 13 describes what love looks like. It does not ask victims to swallow violence. In Taiwan call 113, and call 110 if there is immediate danger.

units.title: Are All Religions the Same?
units.sub: Everyone can tell the story of the blind men and the elephant, but the person who first told it may have meant something different from what you think.

share.v: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father, except through me.

blocks.h: “Religions are like the blind men and the elephant. Everyone is touching the same elephant.” You have surely heard this. Open the early Buddhist scripture, the Udāna, and you find that when the Buddha told the story, his audience was a group of ascetics quarreling over their views. In the story the blind men come to blows over what the elephant is like, while the king watches with amusement. The Buddha’s point was a criticism of arguments in which each side clings to one view. He did not say that all the schools are right.
This ancient fable turns out to be sharper than we remember. So are religions the same or not?
Paul stood in the middle of the Areopagus and said, “You men of Athens, I perceive that you are very religious in all things.
The good intention behind this saying deserves respect

A 2025 Pew Research Center report shows that in 2020 Christians made up about 28.8% of the world’s population, Muslims 25.6%, the religiously unaffiliated 24.2%, Hindus 14.9% and Buddhists 4.1%. Our colleagues, neighbors and family members are often among these numbers. People who say “all religions are the same” mostly want to live together in peace, and that intention is precious.

The philosopher of religion John Hick offered the strongest version of this intuition: there is only one ultimate Reality, and the great religions are different cultures’ different experiences and expressions of it. Every tradition can truly transform lives, so none can claim a monopoly on truth.

But walk into an airport and look at the flights to Tokyo, to Auckland and to Kuala Lumpur. They all have wings, all have flight attendants, and all require you to fasten your seat belt. They are alike, and they are all good. Yet no one therefore says, “It doesn’t matter which flight I take.” Outward similarity does not mean the same destination.
The questions and the answers are actually different

All religions urge people to do good, and that is a real common ground. But ask deeper questions, “What is wrong with humanity, and where is the way out?”, and the answers differ. What follows is a rough sketch and is bound to simplify; the best way to understand more is to ask a serious believer within that tradition.

items: Buddhism: the basic problem of life is suffering, and suffering comes from attachment. It teaches no-self and the pursuit of nirvana, and a creator is generally not central to its faith.
Hinduism: the tradition is extremely diverse, and a common goal is release from the cycle of rebirth, liberation (moksha).

Confucianism: it is concerned with human relationships and self-cultivation in this world. Confucius said, “You do not yet understand life, so how can you understand death?”, putting the emphasis on how to become a person in this life.
Daoism: follow the ineffable Dao: “The Dao that can be spoken is not the constant Dao.” The Dao is not a person who speaks to people.
Islam: it stresses the one God and submission to Him; most Muslims, following Qur’an 4:157, hold that Jesus was not crucified, and they do not accept that Jesus is the Son of God.
Folk religion: worship of many gods and ancestors, often with a focus on peace and protection.
Christianity: the human problem is a broken relationship with God; God Himself became a human being, died in our place on the cross, and rose on the third day.

blocks.h: Whether Jesus died on the cross cannot be both yes and no. Respecting a religion includes listening seriously to what it actually says, rather than smoothing its differences away on its behalf.
Who saw the elephant?

There is something easily overlooked in this fable: where is the storyteller standing? Whoever can say “they each touched only a part” must be able to see the whole elephant. In the Buddha’s version, the ones who see the whole are the king and the Buddha. The nineteenth-century American poet John Godfrey Saxe, in his English poem, used the tale to mock theologians who argue over what they have never seen. So the sentence “no one sees the whole picture” is itself a claim about the whole picture.

items.h: Hick holds that all religions are valid paths in response to the same ultimate Reality. Since every tradition transforms people and is also shaped by culture, none should claim exclusivity. Critics point out that secular values can also transform lives, and that “equal transformation” does not necessarily point to one and the same Reality.
One’s own tradition holds the fullest truth, and other traditions also contain partial, genuine insight.

On conflicting claims, it holds that one side is true. Alvin Plantinga argues that holding such a belief is not necessarily irrational or arrogant. Historical Christianity mostly took this position, while also valuing what is true and good in other traditions.

blocks.h: “You believe what you were born into”

This is one of the most powerful objections: born in Thailand, you will most likely be Buddhist; born in Saudi Arabia, most likely Muslim. Faith is indeed influenced by culture, and that must be honestly admitted. But where an idea comes from is not the same as whether it is true; push the argument all the way and religious pluralism is itself the product of a particular culture. The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy also points out that cultural shaping does not force anyone to adopt pluralism. Why God lets people be born into different circumstances remains a painful question without a complete answer; in the next unit we will keep facing it.

Lesslie Newbigin, a missionary bishop who served for many years in South India, wrote The Gospel in a Pluralist Society late in life. His life reminds us that this question is not a topic from a Western study; it is the everyday matter of Asian Christians among their neighbors.
This topic easily leads to quarrels, so we need all the more to keep facts, interpretations and beliefs apart.
In 2020 about 28.8% of the world was Christian, 25.6% Muslim and 24.2% religiously unaffiliated.

The blind men and the elephant appears in the Buddhist Udāna 6.4, where the Buddha uses it for ascetics who cling to their own views and fight one another. The Jain and Hindu traditions also use it in similar ways, each with a different emphasis.

The religions differ substantially in what they claim about God, humanity and salvation, and some claims are mutually incompatible. Even among pluralists some criticize the idea of presenting the endpoint of all religions as one and the same as overlooking real differences.
The saying that evangelism is one beggar telling another beggar where to find food comes from the 1951 book by the Sri Lankan pastor D. T. Niles, and is often misquoted as “bread.”

“There is only one ultimate Reality, and every religion is a path” and “Jesus is the only way” are both belief claims that go beyond science, and both need reasons. Philosophically, both sides are still arguing.

What is distinctive about the Christian faith is that the ground of salvation is God Himself coming into the world, not human effort. If this is true, its exclusiveness is actually a form of grace: the door is narrow, yet open to everyone.
People are searching, and God is searching too

When Paul came to Athens, he did not smash anyone’s altars. He first looked carefully, saw an altar inscribed “To an unknown god,” and began from there. He even quoted Greek poets. Toward the longing in the human heart he showed respect.
that they should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might reach out for him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us.

Then Paul spoke of something different: this God did not stay up in the clouds waiting for people to climb up. He took the form of a servant, entered human life, and went to the cross. Other roads mostly teach how to go up; the gospel tells how God came down.

who, existing in the form of God, didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men. And being found in human form, he humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, yes, the death of the cross.
So the apostle dared to say this very unmodern thing. The speaker was Peter, a fisherman, and at that moment he was standing on trial before the rulers because of these very words.
There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven that is given among men, by which we must be saved!”

The exclusiveness of truth and human arrogance are two different things. Christians are also people who received grace freely, and have no standing to look down on anyone. And the history of the church does include oppressing others in the name of faith. These things should be admitted and repented of.
Think of a relative or friend whom you respect but whose faith differs from yours. Thank God for that person’s goodness, and pray for a minute for what they need right now.
Reflect: when I talk about faith, am I more like a beggar holding a map, or a top student holding a report card?

Pray: Lord Jesus, You are the way, the truth and the life. Thank You for not waiting for me to climb up, but coming down Yourself to find me. Remove the pride in my heart, so that I dare to speak the truth and also have a gentle heart. Let the friends around me with different faiths see Your kindness in me. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Humility overcomes pride: I did not come to faith because I am smarter. I am a beggar who received grace. The tone of my speech must be worthy of that identity.
The Bible is my standard: I do not smooth over differences by feeling, and I do not push people away by emotion. I go back to Jesus’ own words.
People matter more than tasks: winning an argument and losing a friend is a bad trade. Be a friend first, and then talk about faith.

blocks.h: This week: ask a friend of a different faith, “What matters most to you in your faith?” Listen quietly to the end, do not argue, and thank them sincerely.
Pass it on: “If the religions actually give different answers to life’s questions, which question feels closest to home for you?”
Quiz

quiz.q: In the Buddhist Udāna version, what is the story of the blind men and the elephant used to say?
o: All religions are equally right
It criticizes ascetics who cling to their own views and fight one another
The elephant is a sacred animal
quiz.e: The Buddha used it to describe people who see only one side yet fight one another, and he did not claim that every school is right.

quiz.q: Where did Paul begin when he spoke about the gospel in Athens?
o: Tearing down their altars
Demanding that they be baptized first
An altar inscribed “To an unknown god”
quiz.e: Acts 17:23. He first observed and understood, and then introduced this God.

quiz.q: What does the saying about one beggar telling another beggar remind Christians of?
o: To bring the humility of someone who received grace when sharing the gospel
Christians should give up their possessions
Other religions have no value
quiz.e: The point of Niles’ saying is that the one who tells is also a recipient of grace.

units.title: Can Good People Go to Heaven?
units.sub: The sentence heard most often at a funeral is also the hardest question for the gospel to answer. And then the one you are afraid to ask: what about my ancestors?

share.v: for by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, that no one would boast.

blocks.h: Jesus told a story. One man was a religious model everyone praised: he fasted twice a week and gave a tenth of his income. The other collected taxes for the occupying army, and the whole town looked down on him. Both went up to the temple to pray at the same time.
The ending of the story must have made every listener of that day gasp:
I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but he who humbles himself will be exalted.”
“This man” means the tax collector.
Who sets the standard for “good”?

Mencius held that human nature is originally good, and nearly every culture teaches people to do good. This is a precious shared inheritance of humanity. Christians must first admit honestly that many friends who have not come to faith are kinder and more dependable than Christians. That goodness is real, and the Bible also says that God has written His law in people’s consciences.

The problem is whom we compare ourselves with. We usually compare ourselves with our neighbors, so we feel we are doing all right. Jesus put the greatest commandments as two: love God with all your heart, and love your neighbor as yourself. The verdict “a good person” mostly looks at the second only.

A son is good to the whole village: he repairs the roads, donates schools, and looks after the neighbors, and everyone praises him as a good child. But there is one thing: for twenty years he has not gone home to see his father, and he will not even mention his father’s name, yet no one in the village knows. For this father, the village’s praise does not answer the question. The sin of which the Bible speaks is first of all this kind of break.
for all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God;
The road of works and the road of grace

Most religions and philosophies of life have a method of self-cultivation. These methods teach people to grow in goodness and deserve respect. The most distinctive claim of the Christian faith is that salvation runs in the opposite direction: people cannot climb up to God, so God came down.

Grace is like being adopted. No child is adopted because of a report card. But after being adopted, the child begins to take on the ways of the new father and mother, because he is already part of the family.

So works are not abolished. They simply change place: they are the fruit, not the root. Right after saying “not of works,” Ephesians says in the very next verse that we were “created in Christ Jesus for good works.” In Matthew 25 the righteous who receive a reward even ask back, “Lord, when did we see you hungry”: they were not keeping accounts at all.

The strongest objection is this: a man who did great evil can be saved by believing on his deathbed, while a kind elder cannot. Is that fair? This question deserves to be faced seriously. The Bible’s answer is that evil is not simply erased: on the cross someone paid the price, and real repentance also acknowledges the evil that was done. Whether this is enough to answer the sense of injustice in the human heart, each person must think through for himself, and Christians need not pretend this question is not hard.
What about those who have never heard the gospel?

This is the most honest question, and for many Chinese seekers the most painful: my grandfather and grandmother were kind all their lives and never heard the name of Jesus. What happens to them? There is no single agreed answer within evangelicalism. All the positions agree that salvation comes only through Christ and that God is both just and loving. The difference is in how He brings Christ’s salvation to people.

items.h: A person must hear and believe in Christ in this life to be saved. Ronald Nash represents this view in the 1995 three-views book, and the 2008 volume Faith Comes by Hearing, edited by Morgan and Peterson, also responds to inclusivism. The main grounds are Romans 10:14 and Acts 4:12. Its strength is that it states the urgency of mission most clearly; its difficulty is how to answer for those who never had a chance to hear.

People can be saved only through Christ, but some who never heard His name may have responded to the light God gave them and be saved through Christ. John Sanders represents this view, often pointing to Old Testament saints, Romans 2 and Acts 10. Critics think these passages are not sufficient support, and that the view may weaken mission.

Gabriel Fackre argues that those who have not heard the gospel still have an opportunity after death, often citing 1 Peter 3:19 and 4:6. These passages are hard to interpret; critics such as Nash note that the great majority of evangelicals do not adopt this view, citing Hebrews 9:27.

John Stott held that God has not revealed how He will treat those who have never heard, and he preferred to leave them in the hands of the infinitely loving and just God, hoping that the number of the saved would be large. C. S. Lewis in Mere Christianity expresses a similar humility: we know that no one can be saved except through Christ, but we do not know that only those who know Him can be saved through Him.

blocks.h: The Lausanne Manila Manifesto (1989) is an important document for evangelicals worldwide and leans toward the first position: it says there is no basis for the claim that salvation can be obtained apart from Christ or without explicitly receiving His work, while also repenting of past ignorance and arrogance toward people of other faiths. Here the various views are set side by side, and this unit does not rule between them.
Honoring ancestors: filial piety and the first commandment

Chinese Christians are often misunderstood as people who, once they believe in Jesus, no longer want their ancestors. In fact the fifth commandment plainly tells us, “Honor your father and your mother.” Historically the Catholic Church debated for two to three centuries, and the 1939 instruction Plane Compertum judged that some rites were civil in nature and permitted bowing as a sign of respect. Chinese Protestant churches mostly do not take part in ancestor worship and have developed memorial services; in 2004 Wen Yongsheng put forward contextualized approaches in the Jiandao Journal of Theology, such as “three memorial rites” and an ancestor remembrance chart, with the aim of making the honoring of ancestors more real. Practices differ from church to church, so please discuss this with your pastor. The key is not to pray to the dead, and to be more filial than anyone else.
We mark separately which are historical records and which are theological judgments.

Evangelical theology holds several positions side by side on the fate of those who have not heard the gospel, with books setting them out together (the 1995 three-views volume; the 2008 response from the exclusivist side).

The 1989 Manila Manifesto denies that salvation can be obtained apart from Christ or without explicitly receiving Him, while John Stott in 1988 said he leaned toward leaving the question open. So there are real differences among evangelical leaders.
The 1939 decree Plane Compertum of the Holy See relaxed the earlier prohibition on the Chinese Rites.
People are saved not by their own good deeds but only by the grace of Christ. This is the central claim of the Christian faith, and it lies beyond what history and science can verify.
The final destiny of relatives who have died is not something people can pronounce on God’s behalf. This is a pastoral and theological judgment, not an evasion.
The Judge of all the earth
Abraham once bargained with God over a city. He was not given an explanation of every detail, but he held fast to one thing:
Shouldn’t the Judge of all the earth do right?

For relatives who have died, this verse is where we can stand firm. God loves them more than you do and knows every corner of their lives better than you. The Bible also says that God is “not wishing that anyone should perish,” and that to whom much is given, more is required.
Where justice and grace meet

If God had only justice, no one could stand. If God had only love and ignored justice, the victims’ tears would have been shed for nothing. The place where the two meet is the cross: Christ, “the righteous for the unrighteous,” brings people to God. Heaven is not entered by a score because Someone has already paid the whole price for us.
Because Christ also suffered for sins once, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring you to God, being put to death in the flesh, but made alive in the Spirit,
Heaven is living with God

The Bible describes our hope as a home: God Himself will dwell with people and wipe away every tear. This also makes the seriousness of hell understandable: a person spends a lifetime not wanting God, and God respects that choice. Jesus did speak of an eternal separation (Matthew 25:46), and evangelicals also discuss the details of its nature. But His purpose was clear: God did not send His Son “to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him.”
He will wipe away every tear from their eyes. Death will be no more; neither will there be mourning, nor crying, nor pain any more. The first things have passed away.”
Write down the name of a relative you miss but whose faith you are not sure of. Beside the name write one sentence you would like to say to them, and then bring this paper before God.
Reflect: is my hope built on being better than others, or on what Jesus has done for me? If God asked, “Why should I accept you?”, what would be the first thing I would say?

Pray: Lord, I lay down my own merits and say, like the tax collector, be merciful to me, a sinner. I also place the ancestors and relatives I think about into Your hands. You are just, and You are loving. Let me, while I still have today, tell this love to the family members who are still living. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Humility overcomes pride: “I’m better than he is” is the Pharisee’s prayer. Practice not using other people as your measuring stick.
Letting God be God: other people’s eternal destiny is not ours to judge. Our part is to love and to tell; the judging we leave to the Judge of all the earth.
People matter more than tasks: do not lose a relative by winning a debate about “who gets into heaven.” Filial piety is the best witness.

blocks.h: This week: make a phone call or visit home, and honor an elder who is still living. If Qingming or ancestor rites bring pressure, first talk with the elders about how you would like to express respect, for example by helping clean the grave, offering flowers, or sharing stories about the elder.
Pass it on: “How good do you think a person has to be to be good enough? Who do you think drew that line?”
Quiz

quiz.q: In Jesus’ parable, who “went down to his house justified”?
o: The tax collector who beat his chest and begged for mercy
The Pharisee who fasted and gave
Both men were justified
quiz.e: Luke 18:14. The key is who knows he needs grace.

quiz.q: How does this unit handle the question of those who have never heard the gospel?
o: It is certain that all of them are saved
It is certain that all of them are lost
It sets out the several views within evangelicalism side by side and entrusts them to the just and loving God
quiz.e: All evangelical positions agree that salvation is only through Christ, but they understand differently how God carries it out.

quiz.q: What place do good deeds have in the gospel?
o: A condition for being saved
Fruit that grows after being saved
They do not matter to Christians
quiz.e: Ephesians 2:8-10: salvation is not by works, yet we were created “for good works.”

units.title: How to Begin Walking with God
units.sub: After the universe, the cell and the human heart, the last distance left is from your mouth to your heart. Whether to walk it is your decision.

share.v: that if you will confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.

blocks.h: This app has taken you through the scale of the universe, the precision of the cell and the depths of the human heart. The distance this last unit speaks of is surprisingly short.
But what does it say? “The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart;” that is, the word of faith which we preach:

In 2020 about 2.3 billion people worldwide were counted as Christians. The number itself proves nothing, but every one of those who truly follow Christ once had a first day. Some were in a stadium, some beside a hospital bed, and some were simply alone in a kitchen late at night.
Four sentences of the gospel
The great message of the whole Bible can be condensed into four sentences. They are four sides of one thing, so please read them slowly.
1. God loves you. You are not an accident of the universe. He knows you, and He reaches out first.
For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
2. People have left God. We put ourselves at the center and live in our own way, and this is called sin. Its result is separation from the source of life.
for all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God;
For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
3. Christ died for you, and rose again. God did not make us crawl back by ourselves. Jesus bore the price of our sin and rose from the dead on the third day.
But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

4. Repent and believe. God’s gift has to be received with your own hands. Repentance is a turning around: from “I am in charge” to “Jesus is Lord.” Believing is entrusting yourself to Him, like sitting down on a chair. Studying how the chair is built does not count as sitting.
For with the heart one believes resulting in righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made resulting in salvation.

Imagine receiving a plane ticket that is already paid for. It is real, and it is a free gift. But you still have to set out and board. Repenting and believing is getting up and walking to the gate. It does not matter how messy your luggage is; the ticket was not bought by tidying your luggage.

The Greek word for repentance, metanoia, has to do with a change of mind. The 321 often says “change your mindset, change your life, change how you live,” and that order is in this very word: first the turning, and then life slowly changes afterward.
An honest word: count the cost

The Lausanne Covenant (1974) reminds us that the invitation of the gospel must not hide the cost of discipleship. Jesus Himself said that someone who builds a tower must “first sit down and count the cost.” Believing does not guarantee wealth, healing or a smooth road. What it guarantees is the One who walks with you.
Does it count once you have prayed?

items.h: Many evangelical churches value a clear moment of decision, based on “calling on the name of the Lord” in Romans 10:9-13. A 2012 resolution of the Southern Baptist Convention affirmed the “sinner’s prayer” as one biblical expression of repentance and faith.

Some Christians cannot remember the exact day; they turned to Christ gradually, in a Christian home or through a long period of seeking. Critics remind us that the New Testament gives no fixed template, and worry that people may think all is well once they have recited a prayer.

Traditions understand the role of baptism differently: some see baptism as a witness of obedience after coming to faith, while others (such as Lutherans and Catholics) give it a weightier sacramental meaning. Infant baptism and believer’s baptism have also long been a point of difference.

blocks.h: Most evangelicals would agree: a prayer text is not a magic spell, and the Southern Baptist resolution explicitly denies that it takes effect by being recited. What matters is whether the heart truly turns to Christ, and that turning will bear fruit in the days ahead.
This step is a response of faith. It has a historical basis, and it also has a part that science cannot decide for you.
The summary of the gospel that Paul recorded in 1 Corinthians (generally dated to the 50s AD) is, as he himself says, a tradition he received (15:3).

Scholars’ estimates of when the tradition in 1 Corinthians 15:3-7 took shape average about five years after Jesus’ death (some argue for even earlier), and even the skeptical scholar Gerd Lüdemann regards it as a very early tradition. But this shows that the earliest message is early; for the evaluation of the resurrection itself, see Jesus Hall.

The “sinner’s prayer” is not a fixed New Testament template. The 2012 Southern Baptist resolution affirms it as a biblical expression, while denying that it is a magic spell that works by recitation, and opposing manipulative use of it.

Billy Graham suggested that people reading the Bible for the first time begin with the Gospel of John, then read Acts, then the letters of John and Philippians, and then Romans. This is pastoral advice, and there are other reasonable ways to read.

God reconciles people to Himself in Christ, and people respond by faith. This is the core of the Christian faith. It cannot be proved by experiment; it can only be freely answered by each person, on the strength of evidence, testimony and the light of the Holy Spirit.
He came looking for you first

You thought you were the one searching for God, and only when you got here did you find that someone had been waiting all along. Jesus described God as a father: while the son was still far away, the father ran to him.
He arose and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion, and ran, fell on his neck, and kissed him.
The eternal power and wisdom that this whole app has seen now has a face: hands with nail marks. The One who created the universe is also the One who went to the cross for you.
Death is not the last word
The heart of the gospel is something that has already happened. Paul said this was what he passed on “first of all”:

For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, that he was buried, that he was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
Because He lives, someone hears your prayer, and someone walks with you into tomorrow.
He who comes to me I will in no way throw out.
Find a quiet place. You do not need any special posture, and you do not need anyone beside you. If you like, you can read aloud. No one will be recording, and no one will rush you.

Reflect: imagine that Father seeing you from far away and starting to run toward you. What is your first reaction? Do you want to hide? Do you want to cry? Or do you want to ask, “Is it really all right?” You can tell Him any of these directly.

Pray (a model prayer of decision; if these are the words in your heart, you can read them as your own): Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for loving me. I admit that I am a sinner. I have been living my own way and have left You. Please forgive me. I believe that Jesus Christ is Your Son, that He died on the cross for my sins and rose from the dead on the third day. Today I am willing to turn to You and receive Jesus as my Savior and the Lord of my life. Holy Spirit, come into my heart and help me follow You every day. In Jesus’ name, amen.

Pray (if you are not ready yet, you can read this one): God, if You are really there, I am not sure, but I want to know. Let me come to know You, help me to search honestly, and help my unbelief. If Jesus is truly the One You sent, please let me see. In Jesus’ name, amen.
Both of these are real prayers. If you read the first one, welcome! If you read the second, or if you prayed nothing at all today, God has not closed the door on you, and this app is still here too.
321 Life Application

items: Let Jesus reign: the most basic change in coming to faith is that the steering wheel of your life changes hands. Every morning say one sentence: “Lord, today You are in charge.”
The Bible is my standard, the Holy Spirit is my guide: from today, with every decision large or small, ask: what does the Bible say? How is the Holy Spirit guiding?

920 and selflessness: take the nearest relationship as your training ground (the 2), lay down the “I must win” self (the 0), and slowly bear the fruit of the Spirit (the 9). “It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me” is a lifelong lesson, and you do not have to graduate today.

blocks.h: If you are just beginning, walk like this from here

items: Tell a Christian: today or tomorrow, tell a Christian you trust. If you do not know anyone, you can find us at Kingdom 321 Air Fellowship (YouTube channel @kingdom321air).
Read a little Bible every day: start with the Gospel of John, one chapter a day, and each time ask yourself: what does this passage show me about Jesus?
Talk with God every day: as you would talk with a father. No need to polish your words, and no need for a script.

Join a spiritual family: find a church that takes the Bible as its standard and Christ as its center, or begin by joining the online gatherings of Kingdom 321 Air Fellowship. The Air Fellowship is a bridge; if there is a healthy church near your home, we also encourage you to attend in person.
Be baptized: when you are ready, talk with a pastor about baptism, which is the sign of publicly declaring that you follow Christ.

Mind your safety and freedom: a healthy church does not control you or pressure you for money. If believing would bring conflict, or even legal risk, in your family or where you live, please first consult a pastor you trust, and there is no need to rush to go public.

blocks.h: This week: read John chapter 1, and write down today’s decision (a decision, seeking, or still thinking), with the date. If you would like to talk, find a Christian friend and have a cup of coffee.

Want to learn more: John Stott’s 1958 book Basic Christianity is a commonly used evangelical introduction, and for decades it has helped many seekers sort out who Christ is, what sin is, and what the cross accomplished.
Pass it on: “If there were a God who really loves you, what is the first question you would ask Him?”
Quiz

quiz.q: Which of the following gives the most accurate order and content of the four sentences of the gospel?
o: Do good, store up merit, practice discipline, ascend to heaven
God loves people, people have left God, Christ died and rose, repent and believe
God is angry, people are afraid, give offerings, be blessed
quiz.e: John 3:16, Romans 3:23, 5:8 and 10:9-10 string these four sentences together.

quiz.q: What is this unit’s position on the prayer of decision?
o: Once it is recited, every problem is guaranteed to be solved
It must use a fixed text to count
A prayer text is not a magic spell; what matters is that the heart truly turns to Christ
quiz.e: The New Testament has no fixed template. Prayer is one way of expressing repentance and faith, not magic.

quiz.q: If you are not ready today, what does this unit suggest?
o: You can begin with an honest prayer of seeking, and take it slowly
You do not need to think about it any more
Force yourself to recite the prayer of decision so that no one asks you questions
quiz.e: God does not apply pressure, and seeking is a real step too. Jesus said, “Seek, and you will find.”

questions.q: What am I really living for?
I am hurting so much. Where is God?
I’m a good person. Why would I need Jesus?
I want to begin. What is the first step?
If God is good, why is there evil?

sub: From the meaning of life to the first step of walking with God: twelve units for the deepest questions of the heart.
